recommended_timing: after Wails v3 reaches a release version, not on beta.18. The spike shows the migration works and is small; what it cannot show is what a beta changes before it ships, and the desktop application is the surface a v1.0 support claim rests on.
question: can the Notrios window move from Wails v2 to v3 without giving anything up?
answer: yes, and it gets lighter. The prototype renders the entire real interface -- the real service handler, the real frontend bundle, the real /api/v1 -- behind the full native menu, and links half as many Go modules as the v2 shell.

builds.note: the two binaries are not the same program: the v2 one is the whole notrios command and the prototype is a shell plus the service, so the sizes are not a comparison of the frameworks

frontend_binding_convention.note: window.go.main.X.Y does not exist in v3; these are what a migration rewrites

capabilities.cost: a field moved; the http.Handler type is identical, so the whole frontend and every /api/v1 request route exactly as before
mechanical; submenus, separators, the Edit role and every accelerator survive, F11 included
a typed helper becomes a string; the strings were accepted as written
methods on the window rather than functions taking a context, which removes the captured appCtx the v2 shell threads through every menu callback
a shape change: the callback no longer receives a context, so the dialog it asks has to reach the app another way

capabilities.v3: Dialog.Question(); each button carries OnClick; Show() returns nothing
capabilities.cost: THE ONE THAT NEEDS THOUGHT. The unsaved-work guard has to decide now, so it must wait for a callback: the prototype blocks on a channel with a timeout and fails closed, which is what production already does when a dialog cannot be shown

capabilities.v3: @wailsio/runtime Call.ByName, or modules from `wails3 generate bindings`
capabilities.cost: THE REAL COST. window.go does not exist in v3 -- zero occurrences in its compiled runtime -- and the frontend has 11 references across 7 files. Two of them are the accessors in web/src/desktop.ts; the other five reach for window.go directly and would move behind those accessors as part of the same change

v3_offers_what_v2_had_no_answer_for: SingleInstance, which is how a second launch could hand a notrios:// link to the running window instead of opening a second one
FileAssociations, the same question for files
KeyBindings at application level, rather than only through the menu
iOS and Android options, which are not a reason to migrate the desktop: the roadmap's mobile client is Flutter over the C ABI, and H11 proved that path on an emulator the day before this ran
what_this_did_not_measure: calling a bound service from JavaScript. The frontend still speaks the v2 convention, so the prototype proves services register, not that they answer
packaging a .deb against v3. dpkg-shlibdeps computes Depends from the binary so it should follow, but nothing here built one
the desktop journey harness under v3, which drives menus with xdotool
Windows and macOS, which have no toolchain on this machine and are post-v1.0 anyway
deep links end to end; SingleInstance and FileAssociations were read from the API, not exercised
risks: beta.18 is a beta, and v3's own documentation calls the desktop beta. A release is expected within the month, which is the reason to prepare rather than to move now
GTK4 and webkitgtk-6.0 replace GTK3 and webkit2gtk-4.1. Every documented install line changes -- six places say libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev today -- and so does what an installed .deb depends on
the editor is md-editor-rt inside a webview; a different webview engine is a rendering risk the spike did not exercise beyond loading the page
rollback: delete performance/v0.8-h10/prototype. The prototype is a nested module, so the production go.mod never learned v3 exists -- verified, not asserted: production_untouched=yes
boundaries_held: the production shell was not migrated
Wails v2 was not removed and still builds and runs
H6 and H7 gained no dependency on v3
